monitored_items.characteristic: Order-to-handoff time (handoff_minutes -- charter C1, the primary CTQ)
monitored_items.frequency: Daily during the weekday 7:00-10:00 peak, entered at close of peak
monitored_items.frequency_reason: ~55 orders flow per semester peak and the July baseline showed a shift can show up inside a single morning (the Aug class-break pileups); daily entry against the frozen band catches drift within a day or two instead of three weeks late, and it reuses the sampling the limits were frozen from
monitored_items.how_measured: Register order-paid timestamp to name call, tenths of a minute, every 4th espresso order (12 per peak) -- the T-11 operational definition the whole project has used, unchanged
monitored_items.where: Register POS + pickup-counter tally sheet, campus coffee bar

monitored_items.characteristic: Drink remake rate (remakes per 100 orders) -- the charter's consequential guardrail
monitored_items.frequency: Weekly roll-up, each Friday at close
monitored_items.frequency_reason: At the improved rate (~2.3 per 100) a single morning's 55 orders sees one remake on a good day -- daily rates are too noisy to act on; a Friday roll-up over ~275 peak orders gives a rate worth reading, and a bad week still surfaces within five service days
monitored_items.how_measured: Barista waste-sheet remake tally divided by the POS order count, x100, rolled up weekly -- same waste sheet the Q2 COPQ priced
monitored_items.where: Espresso-station waste sheet + POS daily count export

monitored_items.characteristic: Improve-change adherence: batch milk steaming + marked-cup sequencing, and the pre-peak grinder dial-in / standby-swap routine, done to standard

monitored_items.frequency_reason: Method backsliding is the failure mode the chart cannot see directly and it grows in days, not months -- twice-weekly catches a lapse inside a week while staying light enough that it actually keeps happening
monitored_items.how_measured: Five-point spot-check against SOP coffee-standard-work v1's changed-from-prior steps (pair scan done, ticket order held, front-of-rail grab, dial-in logged before 7:00, refill re-dial logged), pass/fail per point, unannounced
monitored_items.where: Espresso station during the live peak

artifact.notes: What keeps the fix alive after the project ends, written the day the limits froze and kept current through the check-ins (as_of 2026-10-09). Three monitored items: the primary CTQ (handoff minutes, judged against coffee-control-chart's frozen band), the charter's remake-rate guardrail, and the changed method itself -- the fix is monitored, not just the outcome, because when the number drifts you need to know whether the method lapsed or stopped working. Every item has a named owner who accepted the role on the 2026-09-22 handoff walk (Priya and Marcus signed the plan sheet; both are charter team), a frequency with a stated reason, and an OCAP whose first response is always investigate-the-method before touching anything -- the investigate-then-respond steps name the two changed methods (batch-steam/sequencing and the grinder dial-in/swap) because those are the two things that can silently lapse. Training rows point at the T-24 SOP (coffee-standard-work v1) by artifact id and every row carries a verification that would actually verify (observed demonstration or a run of the spot-check, signed off) -- told-about-it is not on the list. Weekly check-ins are the chase this phase is famous for skipping: two are due so far, both answered on their due dates with the week's spot-pair entries scored by the engine against the FROZEN band (both pass, all entries inside 3.029-6.770); next_due is engine-computed, never typed. Check-in entries are the first and last sampled order of each service morning that week (2 x 4 mornings in the short week of Sep 22, 2 x 5 after) -- the full 12-a-day stream lives on the chart itself; the check-in is the weekly is-it-holding roll-up.

action_steps: First response -- investigate before adjusting: check the two changed methods for that morning -- was the batch-steam/sequencing followed (pair scan, ticket order, front-of-rail grab) and was the grinder dial-in done and logged before 7:00? Run mi-method's five-point check on the spot and re-time the next three sampled orders.

Containment: if the queue is backing up, move the second barista onto cup-sequencing and milk while the signal morning runs out, limit batching to same-milk pairs only, and log the morning's order count -- a demand surge is a possible special cause, not a reason to widen limits.
Never adjust the process on a single inside-the-band wiggle -- that is common cause, and chasing it adds variation (tampering).
ocap_entries.escalation_trigger: Two signals inside one rolling week, or any single morning mean above 6.77
ocap_entries.trigger_signal: Any point beyond the frozen band (3.029 / 6.770) or a rule-4 run of 8 consecutive points one side of the 4.899 center on the daily entries

action_steps: First response -- read the waste sheet's reason column before changing anything: if re-pulls dominate, audit the grinder card for skipped morning dial-ins or hopper refills without a re-dial (the round-2 method lapsing); if wrong-drink remakes dominate, audit the pair scan and ticket-order discipline (the round-1 method lapsing).

Containment: swap to the standby grinder and re-dial the primary off-peak; if wrong-drink remakes are the driver, drop to single-drink build for the rest of the week and re-train the pair scan before batching resumes.
ocap_entries.escalation_trigger: Rate above 3.6 per 100 two consecutive weekly roll-ups
ocap_entries.trigger_signal: Weekly remake rate above 3.6 per 100 -- the Q2 baseline level, the guardrail's no-worse line

action_steps: First response: same-day refresh with the barista on the failed step, walked against the SOP's written standard for that step (coffee-standard-work v1), not from memory.
Containment: laminated SOP card goes back up at the station and Priya works the rail alongside the next peak until a clean five-point check passes.
ocap_entries.escalation_trigger: The same step failing again after a refresh
ocap_entries.trigger_signal: Any spot-check point failed on two consecutive checks, or a week passing with fewer than two checks done
